body.proof_tex:
We give the deterministic charging and the probability calculation.  They are conditional on \(\mathcal F_1\), so \(\eta\) is fixed and independent of the second-half observations by independent sampling.  Write \(P_X=P\circ X^{-1}\).  For \(x=(0,s)\), \(h=\eta(x)\), and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), write
\[
 A(x,t)=A_t\cap B_2(x,h),\qquad p(x,t)=P\{X\in A(x,t)\}.
\]
The base-mass condition gives \(p(x,t)\geq a_P(x,h)>0\).  Conditional on all scores, independence and the conditional sub-Gaussian assumption imply
\[
 E_P\!\left[\exp\!\left\{\lambda
 \sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\right\}
 \middle|X_1,\ldots,X_n,\mathcal F_1\right]
 \leq \exp\!\left\{\frac{\lambda^2\sigma^2N_2(A)}2\right\}       \tag{M3}
\]
for every selected set \(A\), where \(N_2(A)=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\).  Exponential Markov applied to \(\lambda\) and \(-\lambda\), followed by minimization in \(\lambda\), gives
\[
 P\!\left\{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A\}\right|
 >\sigma\sqrt{2N_2(A)z}\,\middle|X_1,\ldots,X_n,\mathcal F_1\right\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                        \tag{M4}
\]

We next prove the multiscale count used to spend the tail probabilities in \((\mathrm{M4})\).  Associate with \(A(x,t)\) the untruncated boundary interval
\[
 I(x)=[s-h,s+h].
\]
For centers on the vertical line, \(I(x)\subseteq I(x')\) is equivalent to
\(|s-s'|+h\leq h'\), and this implies
\(B_2(x,h)\subseteq B_2(x',h')\).  At one fixed \(h\) and in one dyadic mass cell with ceiling \(u\), choose greedily, from left to right, a maximal \(h/2\)-separated list of centers and call them the fixed-scale roots.  Every remaining center is within \(h/2\) of a root.  For a fixed score \((r_i,s_i)\) with \(|r_i|\leq h\), membership as the center coordinate varies is the indicator of
\([s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}]\); otherwise it is identically zero.  Thus a left-to-right sweep through a cluster charges the score with at most one entrance and one exit.  The ordered root list splits into its odd and even sublists, each of which is \(h\)-separated.  Hence, for every \(u\geq0\), the number of fixed-scale roots whose centers satisfy \(a_P(x,h)\leq u\) is at most
\[
 2\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}.                                                \tag{M5}
\]

For completeness, here is the varying-radius construction.  First order the selected intervals by decreasing dyadic radius, then by left endpoint, then by right endpoint, retaining one representative for each selected second-half membership pattern.  Attach an interval to the least earlier interval containing it; if none exists, declare it a root.  For the half-disks on one fixed treatment side, two noncoincident circular boundary arcs whose centers lie on \(B\) intersect at most once: subtracting their two squared-circle equations leaves an affine equation in the boundary coordinate.  Consequently the exposed left arcs and exposed right arcs of the noncontained children are each endpoint-monotone.  Sweep these two lists separately.  Membership of any fixed score in a swept list is consecutive, because a second entrance after an exit would force two intersections of the corresponding exposed arcs.  On each list, cut whenever the \(P_X\)-mass newly entered or left since the preceding cut first exceeds \(2^{-r}u\), where \(u\) is the parent's mass ceiling.  Every set in the list is contained in the parent and every score enters and leaves at most once, so each list has total entered-plus-left mass at most \(2u\).  Thus at charge depth \(r\) there are at most
\[
 2^{r+2}\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}                                         \tag{M6}
\]
charged blocks issued from the roots in \((\mathrm{M5})\), and every block has \(P_X\)-mass at most \(2^{-r}u\).  For roots of different radii in the same mass and variance cell, let \(h_*\) be the smallest radius.  Monotonicity of ball mass gives
\(a_P(x,h_*)\leq a_P(x,h_x)\leq u\) for every root center.  Greedy clustering at distance \(h_*/2\), followed by odd/even splitting, leaves at most
\(2\{1\vee J_P(h_*,u)\}\) clusters; the two exposed-arc sweeps control all roots inside a cluster.  The root having radius \(h_*\) belongs to the selected family, so the supremum in \((\mathrm{M7})\) contains the logarithmic charge for this common packing count.  Intervals of equal endpoint or equal radius are assigned by the displayed deterministic tie order, so every selected pattern is charged exactly once.  An infinite center family causes no difficulty: on fixed second-half scores it has finitely many membership patterns, and monotone convergence passes from these finite representatives to the supremum.

Let
\[
 \Lambda(x)=1+\log\!\left(
 e\left\{1\vee J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h)\}\right)\right\}\right),
 \qquad
 R=\sup_{x\in B}\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(x)}{n_2a_P(x,h)}}.       \tag{M7}
\]
For each cell, either its expected count is at least \(64\Lambda(x)\), or its normalized oracle scale is already bounded below by a numerical multiple of \(\sigma\):
\[
 n_2a_P(x,h)\geq64\Lambda(x)
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda(x)}{n_2a_P(x,h)}}>\frac\sigma8.       \tag{M8}
\]
Peel the roots simultaneously by the dyadic values of \(h\), of \(a_P(x,h)\), and of \(p(x,t)/a_P(x,h)\).  In a cell with mass ceiling \(u\), equations \((\mathrm{M5})\)--\((\mathrm{M6})\) and the definition of \(\Lambda\) show that the number of depth-\(r\) blocks is at most
\(2^{r+2}e^{\Lambda-1}\).  A depth-\(r\) block has variance proxy at most \(2^{-r}n_2u\sigma^2\).  Applying \((\mathrm{M4})\) to its increment at threshold
\[
 C\sigma\sqrt{n_2u\{\Lambda+z\}}
\]
therefore spends at most
\[
 2^{r+3}e^{\Lambda-1}
 \exp\{-c2^r(\Lambda+z)\}.                                         \tag{M9}
\]
Summing \((\mathrm{M9})\) over \(r\geq0\) is at most \(C e^{-cz}\).  Passing from one side-mass cell to the next multiplies the numerator standard deviation by \(2^{1/2}\) and the reciprocal count by \(2^{-1}\); hence its contribution to an average is multiplied by \(2^{-1/2}\).  Summing \(\sum_{j\geq0}2^{-j/2}<\infty\) pays all side-mass severity cells.  The dyadic radius forest is already included in \((\mathrm{M6})\): contained intervals are increments paid by \((\mathrm{M9})\), while incomparable radii in a common mass-variance cell are clustered at their smallest radius and paid by its packing count.  Moving to a smaller variance cell gives the same \(2^{-1/2}\) factor.  Consequently neither the number of radii nor the number of mass cells appears in the threshold.

Apply the same forest calculation to the centered Bernoulli variables
\(\mathbf 1\{X_i\in A\}-P_X(A)\).  On the first alternative in \((\mathrm{M8})\), the Bernoulli exponential-moment bound implies that the forest probability of
\(N_2(A)<n_2P_X(A)/2\) is summable, because a cell having packing charge \(e^{\Lambda-1}\) has lower-tail probability at most \(e^{-8\Lambda}\).  On the complementary event, every selected set has
\[
 N_2(A)\geq \tfrac12n_2P_X(A),                                     \tag{M10}
\]
On \((\mathrm{M10})\), divide the increment bounds from \((\mathrm{M9})\) by \(N_2(A)\), telescope along each root-to-leaf path, and use \((\mathrm{M7})\).  On the lower-count complement, peel the positive counts into
\(2^{-d-1}n_2P_X(A)<N_2(A)\leq2^{-d}n_2P_X(A)\).  The Bernoulli lower-tail exponent is still at least \(c n_2P_X(A)\), whereas \((\mathrm{M4})\)'s average threshold grows only as \(2^{d/2}\); summing in \(d\) gives the same constant multiple of \(R\).  Cells in the second alternative of \((\mathrm{M8})\) are handled by the same positive-count peeling starting at \(d=0\); their oracle scale is at least \(\sigma/8\), and the factor \(e^{\Lambda-1}\) is paid by the \(\Lambda\) term in \((\mathrm{M9})\).  Thus, for every \(z\geq1\),
\[
 P\!\left\{
 \sup_{x,t:N_t^{(2)}(x,h)>0}
 \frac{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A(x,t)\}\right|}{N_t^{(2)}(x,h)}
 >CR(1+\sqrt z)\,\middle|\mathcal F_1\right\}
 \leq Ce^{-cz}.                                                      \tag{M11}
\]
Finally, integrate \((\mathrm{M11})\), using
\(E Z=\int_0^\infty P(Z>v)\,dv\) for a nonnegative random variable and
\(\int_1^\infty e^{-cz}\,dz<\infty\).  This proves \((\mathrm{M2})\), since its displayed additive remainder is nonnegative.  Every division used \((\mathrm{M10})\), a peeled positive count, or the explicit positive-count restriction, and every logarithm is defined because of \(1\vee J_P\).
body.justification: The interval forest makes the selected-bandwidth stochastic argument load-bearing and checkable.
